family: General relativity, cosmology, and dynamical astronomy
family_notes:
SCOPE OF THE FAMILY. This family contains five structurally different things that all get called "units" in papers, and an engine that conflates them will be silently wrong.

(1) CONVENTION (true unit system): a dimensionful combination of universal constants is set to 1. Symbols disappear from equations; dimensions collapse. Equation FORMS change. This is what the generator table models. Rows 1-10 here.

(2) UNIT CHOICE: a differently-sized member of an unchanged dimension (kpc vs m, M_sun vs kg, day vs s, Jy vs W m^-2 Hz^-1, erg vs J). Generator set EMPTY. Equation forms byte-identical to SI/CGS; only numbers change; translation is one multiplicative scale per base dimension. Astronomy is dominated by these and they are NOT unit systems. Rows 13, 19, 21, 23, 25, 26 (and the gravity sector of 12).

(3) NORMALIZATION: dimensionally behaves exactly like a generator, but the scale is a property of the SYSTEM UNDER STUDY, not a constant of nature (M_BH, M_total, R_vir, Plummer a, R_0, v_c, H_0, M_unit). The linear-algebra restoration works unchanged, but the numeric value must be bound per-paper from prose. Rows 4, 5, 6, 16, 17, 18, 20, 22.

(4) PARAMETERIZED RESCALING: a DIMENSIONLESS factor hidden in each symbol, with a per-symbol exponent. Invisible to dimensional analysis. Little h (row 14) and the TDB/TCB time-scale rescaling (row 23). These are the strongest argument for the per_symbol_rescalings field: no dimension check recovers them.

(5) LOGARITHMIC SCALE: magnitudes, dex, decibels (row 24). Outside the formalism entirely; must be refused, not approximated.

Papers routinely mix all five in one sentence: "we set G = c = 1, quote masses in M_sun, distances in Mpc, fluxes in mJy, and the host has M_r = -21.3 + 5 log h." The engine must therefore track a convention (generator set) and a display-unit map INDEPENDENTLY, not a single system label.

=== WHICH SYSTEMS ARE MUTUALLY INDISTINGUISHABLE FOR GRAVITY-ONLY CONTENT ===

CLUSTER A - literally identical gravitational equations, always:
  #1 Geometrized (G=c=1, mass in length); #1-alias Geometrized-second (mass in seconds); #2 Geometrized-Gaussian (gravity sector); #3 Geometrized-Heaviside-Lorentz (gravity sector); #4 Black-hole scale units (G=c=M=1); #5 NR code units (G=c=M_sun=1); #6 GRMHD code units (gravity sector); #10 Planck units (gravity sector).
All write G_mn + L g_mn = 8 pi T_mn, S = (1/16pi) int R sqrt(-g), ds^2 = -(1-2M/r)dt^2 + ..., T_H = 1/(8 pi M), S_BH = A/4. A gravity-only equation CANNOT distinguish them. What separates them is never equation form:
  - #1 vs #1-alias vs #5: only the NUMBERS quoted (1.4766 km vs 4.9255e-6 s vs 1).
  - #4/#5/#6 differ from #1 only if M (or M_sun) appears explicitly; a paper writing r/M or "M = 1" reveals them.
  - #2 vs #3 vs #1 differ only once charge appears (Q^2/r^2 vs Q^2/(4 pi r^2)).
  - #10 differs from #1 only once hbar appears (hbar = 1 vs hbar = l_P^2 = 2.612e-70 m^2).
A classifier must return the whole cluster with a confidence spread, never a single label, when the input is a vacuum metric or a matter-free Einstein equation.

CLUSTER B - identical in VACUUM only (the worst case):
  Cluster A UNION {#8 reduced-Planck 8piG=c=1, #9 kappa=1 classical, #11 with kappa bound to 1}.
In vacuum, R_mn = L g_mn, Schwarzschild, Kerr, geodesics, quasinormal modes, Regge-Wheeler/Teukolsky, and vacuum post-Newtonian expansions are IDENTICAL between geometrized (G=c=1) and reduced-Planck (8piG=c=1). The 8 pi becomes visible only when T_mn, rho, p, an action prefactor, or a Lambda-to-rho_Lambda conversion appears. RECOMMENDED BEHAVIOR: for vacuum-only input, refuse to choose between G=c=1 and 8piG=c=1 and ask; the restored SI form differs by 8 pi in every matter-coupled downstream equation.

CLUSTER C - Newtonian G=1 systems, identical equation forms:
  #17 Henon/N-body (G=M=1, E=-1/4); #18 Model/Plummer units (G=M=a=1); #20 galpy/AGAMA natural units (R_0=v_c=1); #22 astrodynamics canonical units (mu=1); #21-variant heliocentric canonical with k=1 (time unit 58.132441 d).
All write laplacian(Phi) = 4 pi rho and rdotdot_i = -sum_j m_j (r_i-r_j)/|r_i-r_j|^3 with G absent. The third normalization (E=-1/4 vs R_v=1 vs a=1 vs v_c=1 vs DU=R_ref) is stated in PROSE and appears in no equation. Per-equation these are indistinguishable; only the quoted crossing time (2 sqrt 2), the Plummer scale (3 pi/16), the number 806.8 s, or the methods section separates them.

CLUSTER D - zero-generator unit choices, equation forms identical to SI/CGS:
  #12 (gravity sector), #13, #19, #21 (k-explicit form), #23, #25, #26, and largely #14, #15.
G and c stay explicit. Classify as "display units" and never attempt constant restoration - there is nothing to restore.

DECISION PROCEDURE, priority order:
  a. Read the Einstein-equation / action prefactor. Most informative single token.
       G_mn = (8 pi G/c^4) T_mn  -> no generators (SI/CGS)
       G_mn = (8 pi G/c^2) T_mn  -> no generators, T is a MASS density (Einstein 1916)
       G_mn = 8 pi G T_mn        -> c = 1 only (#7)
       G_mn = 8 pi T_mn          -> Cluster A
       G_mn = T_mn               -> 8 pi G = c = 1 (#8/#9)
       G_mn = kappa T_mn         -> kappa symbolic (#11); MUST bind kappa per-paper
       Action prefactor 1/(16 pi G) -> c=1; c^4/(16 pi G) with d^4x = dt d^3x -> SI; c^3/(16 pi G) with d^4x = c dt d^3x -> SI; 1/(16 pi) -> Cluster A; M_Pl^2/2 or 1/2 -> #8.
  b. If vacuum-only, stop and report Cluster B ambiguity.
  c. Check whether hbar and k_B appear (separates #10 from #1, #8 from #9).
  d. Check the Maxwell normalization (-1/(16 pi) F^2 = Gaussian; -1/4 F^2 = Heaviside-Lorentz).
  e. Check quoted numbers for the residual scale (km / s / M_sun / dimensionless).

TRAPS THAT STRESS OR BREAK THE GENERATOR-TABLE SCHEMA:
  T1. Little h (#14): a dimensionless per-symbol factor with a DIFFERENT exponent per quantity (lengths h^-1, masses h^-1, densities h^+2, number densities h^+3, P(k) h^-3, luminosities h^-2, absolute magnitudes +5 log h, times h^-1, velocities h^0). No generator table expresses this; it needs a per-quantity exponent map. The clearest needs_symbol_rescaling case in the family.
  T2. TDB/TCB (#23): two quantities both called "the second" and two both called "the au", differing by L_B = 1.550519768e-8. Dimensional analysis is blind.
  T3. Scale-factor dimensions (#15): whether a is dimensionless (a_0 = 1, k has dimension L^-2) or carries length (k = 0, +-1 exactly) changes the DIMENSION of k, of comoving coordinates, and of conformal time. Two identical-looking FRW metrics carry different dimension assignments.
  T4. kappa as a named combination (#11): not a generator and not a unit choice, but a SYMBOL ALIAS with three literature expansions of DIFFERENT dimension ((-1,-1,2,0,0) for 8piG/c^4 vs (-1,1,0,0,0) for 8piG/c^2 vs (-1,3,-2,0,0) for 8piG). Handle with an alias table plus a dimension-driven disambiguation pass keyed on the declared units of T_00. This is the one place where dimension-checking genuinely DISAMBIGUATES rather than merely validates.
  T5. Per-object generators (#4,#5,#6,#16,#17,#18,#20,#22): M, M_total, R_vir, a, R_0, v_c, H_0, M_unit are not constants of nature. Restoration emits a SYMBOL, not a number, until bound.
  T6. Residual free scale: G = c = 1 fixes only 2 of 3 mechanical base dimensions, so one length scale stays free. "Geometrized units" determines equation form, NOT numeric conversion. Adding M (or M_sun, or R_vir) closes the system.
  T7. Logarithmic units (#24) and hybrid instrument units (Jy/beam, K km/s, mag/arcsec^2) that hide a beam solid angle, a line width, or an angular area. Refuse with a specific message.
  T8. The c^3 vs c^4 Einstein-Hilbert prefactor, depending on whether d^4x means dt d^3x or c dt d^3x. Dimensionally detectable ([S] = M L^2 T^-1) and worth auto-checking.
  T9. M_sun is not a primitive. IAU 2015 B3 recommends quoting GM_sun (nominal 1.3271244e20 m^3 s^-2, ~1e-10) not M_sun (limited by G to ~2e-5). Store GM_sun as primary; every M_sun-in-kg conversion carries a hidden G dependence.
  T10. Signature and curvature-sign conventions (MTW's [S1,S2,S3]) and Landau-Lifshitz's k for Newton's constant (colliding with curvature index k, FRW k, and Boltzmann k_B) are not unit issues but wreck naive fingerprinting. Keep sign conventions as an orthogonal field.
  T11. Gravitational-radius ambiguity: r_g = GM/c^2 in most GR literature but 2GM/c^2 in parts of the accretion-disk/X-ray-binary literature. A factor of 2, invisible dimensionally, changing a quoted ISCO between 6 r_g and 3 r_g.
  T12. Lambda placement: Lambda (L^-2) vs rho_Lambda = Lambda c^2/(8 pi G) vs Lambda in eV^4 vs dimensionless Omega_Lambda. Four objects, one word.
  T13. Reduced vs unreduced Planck mass differ by sqrt(8 pi) = 5.013 (2.435e18 GeV vs 1.22089e19 GeV). Purely numeric, dimensionally invisible, the most common single error in inflation-paper translation.

systems.name: Little-h units (h^{-1} Mpc, h^{-1} M_\odot, h^2 densities)
systems.used_in: Galaxy surveys and clustering (SDSS, BOSS, eBOSS, DES, 2dF), cosmological N-body and hydrodynamic simulations (Millennium, IllustrisTNG, EAGLE, Bolshoi), halo mass functions and halo catalogues, galaxy luminosity and stellar-mass functions, matter power spectra.

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: x_{[h^{-1}\mathrm{Mpc}]} = h\cdot x_{[\mathrm{Mpc}]}; a value X quoted in h^{-1} Mpc means a physical X/h Mpc
per_symbol_rescalings.why: Distances are inferred from redshifts via D \sim cz/H_0 and so carry an explicit h^{-1}. Quoting in h^{-1} Mpc removes the H_0 uncertainty from the measurement.

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: M_{[h^{-1}M_\odot]} = h\cdot M_{[M_\odot]}
per_symbol_rescalings.why: Dynamical and lensing masses scale as M \sim v^2r/G \sim h^{-1}, inheriting the distance scaling.

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: \rho_{[h^2M_\odot\mathrm{Mpc^{-3}}]} = h^{-2}\rho_{[M_\odot\mathrm{Mpc^{-3}}]}; \ n_{[h^3\mathrm{Mpc^{-3}}]} = h^{-3}n_{[\mathrm{Mpc^{-3}}]}
per_symbol_rescalings.why: Mass density = (h^{-1}M_\odot)/(h^{-1}Mpc)^3 = h^{+2}M_\odot Mpc^{-3}; number density carries h^{+3}. The exponent differs from that of mass or length — which is exactly why a single scale factor cannot express the convention.
Reciprocal of a length, so the h exponent flips sign.

L = 4\pi D_L^2F with D_L \propto h^{-1}, so L \propto h^{-2}.

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: M_{\rm abs}^{(h)} = M_{\rm abs} + 5\log_{10}h, written in papers as 'M_r - 5\log h'
per_symbol_rescalings.why: The logarithmic image of the L \propto h^{-2} scaling: -2.5\log_{10}(h^{-2}) = +5\log_{10}h. A multiplicative rescaling appearing as an ADDITIVE shift because the quantity is logarithmic — the two pathological cases of this family combined in one symbol.

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: t_{[h^{-1}\mathrm{Gyr}]} = h\,t_{[\mathrm{Gyr}]}
per_symbol_rescalings.why: Times scale as H_0^{-1} \propto h^{-1}.

Note also that h is not a unit at all: it encodes an unknown part of a numerical value, which is why some authors argue against the convention outright.

systems.name: Comoving / scale-factor normalization conventions
systems.used_in: All of FRW cosmology. The two variants split roughly along textbook lines: dimensionless a with a_0 = 1 dominates modern observational cosmology and Boltzmann codes; a-as-curvature-radius with k = 0, \pm1 appears in mathematical-relativity treatments and older texts.

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: Variant A: a dimensionless with a_0 \equiv a(t_0) = 1. Variant B: a carries the dimension of LENGTH and equals the curvature radius, with k \in \{-1,0,+1\} exactly. Relation a_A = a_B/R_{\rm curv,0}.
per_symbol_rescalings.why: A genuine change in the DIMENSION of a symbol, not a change of unit size. Two FRW metrics that look character-for-character identical assign different dimensions to a, to the comoving radial coordinate, and to k.

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: Variant A: [k] = L^{-2}, tuple (0,-2,0,0,0), with \Omega_k = -kc^2/(a_0^2H_0^2). Variant B: k is a dimensionless integer in \{-1,0,+1\}.
per_symbol_rescalings.why: Direct consequence of a's dimension. A dimension checker assuming the wrong variant reports a false error on the Friedmann equation, or silently passes an inconsistent one.

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: d\eta = dt/a. Variant A: \eta has dimension of time (or length with c = 1). Variant B: \eta is DIMENSIONLESS.
per_symbol_rescalings.why: Same cascade. In Variant B the metric is ds^2 = a^2(\eta)\left[-d\eta^2 + d\chi^2 + S_k^2(\chi)d\Omega^2\right] with \chi and \eta both dimensionless and all the length carried by a.

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: D_{\rm comoving} = D_{\rm physical}/a = D_{\rm physical}(1+z) in Variant A with a_0 = 1
per_symbol_rescalings.why: Quoted as 'cMpc' versus 'pMpc'. Same dimension, a factor of (1+z) apart, and papers often omit which they mean.

fingerprints: 'we normalize a_0 = 1', 'a(t_0) = 1', 'the scale factor today is unity'
k = 0, \pm1 written as an exact set (Variant B) versus \Omega_k as a continuous fitted parameter (Variant A)
ds^2 = a^2(\eta)\left(-d\eta^2 + \gamma_{ij}dx^idx^j\right)
'cMpc' versus 'pMpc'; 'comoving' versus 'proper'/'physical' attached to a distance or density
comoving number densities 'per comoving Mpc^3'
in Variant A, a derived curvature radius R_{\rm curv} = c/(H_0\sqrt{|\Omega_k|})

benchmark_equations.coulomb: N/A.
benchmark_equations.gauss_law: Cosmological Poisson equation, Variant A: \nabla^2\Phi = 4\pi Ga^2\bar\rho\,\delta, with \nabla taken in comoving coordinates and the a^2 exactly the factor that makes the dimensions work. Getting the power of a wrong here is among the most common errors in perturbation-theory translation.
benchmark_equations.einstein_field: Variant A: H^2 = \dfrac{8\pi G}{3}\rho - \dfrac{kc^2}{a^2} + \dfrac{\Lambda c^2}{3} with [k] = L^{-2} and a dimensionless. Variant B: identical-looking, but k \in \{-1,0,1\} and [a] = L. Both sides have the same dimensions either way, which is why the error is silent.
benchmark_equations.schrodinger_or_dirac: N/A, though the Mukhanov-Sasaki equation v_k'' + \left(c_s^2k^2 - z''/z\right)v_k = 0 inherits the same ambiguity through z = a\sqrt{2\epsilon}M_{\rm Pl} and through whether k is comoving in Mpc^{-1} or in h Mpc^{-1}.

systems.notes: Not a unit system in any conventional sense, but it belongs in the table because it changes the DIMENSION TUPLE assigned to k, \eta and the comoving coordinates — precisely what a dimension checker consumes. Recommend a per-paper boolean 'scale factor dimensionless (a_0 = 1)', defaulting true for post-1990 observational cosmology and flipped on detecting 'k = \pm1'. The comoving-versus-proper distinction is a separate per-quantity flag: same dimensions, a factor (1+z)^{\pm1} or (1+z)^{\pm3} apart, and again invisible to dimensional analysis.

systems.notes: H_0 (and the inflationary H) is not a constant of nature and is not even constant in time, so this is a per-paper normalization rather than a convention. It earns a row because papers state it as if it were a unit system and because it removes H from equations in a way a naive restorer will not undo. Note that H = 1 during inflation is only approximately meaningful (H is slowly varying), so restoring H is not an exact operation — the engine should flag this rather than pretend the substitution is invertible.

systems.name: Henon units (N-body units): G = M = 1, E = -1/4
systems.used_in: Collisional stellar dynamics: globular- and open-cluster N-body simulations (NBODY6, NBODY6++GPU, PeTar), Monte Carlo cluster codes (MOCCA, CMC), core-collapse and mass-segregation studies, dynamical binary formation and black-hole subsystem work.

benchmark_equations.coulomb: N/A: purely gravitational stellar dynamics. The formal analogue is the pairwise potential -m_im_j/r_{ij}, structurally a Coulomb potential with attractive sign and 'charge' equal to mass.
benchmark_equations.gauss_law: N/A (no electromagnetic sector). Gravitational analogue: \nabla^2\Phi = 4\pi\rho, and \oint\mathbf{g}\cdot d\mathbf{A} = -4\pi M_{\rm enc}.
benchmark_equations.einstein_field: N/A: Newtonian gravity. Post-Newtonian terms, when added for black-hole binaries inside clusters, carry explicit 1/c^n and c is NOT 1 here — a genuine mixed-convention hazard, since c has the numerical value \sqrt{R_{\rm v}c^2/(GM)} \sim 10^{3}-10^{4} in Henon units. Equation of motion: \ddot{\mathbf{r}}_i = -\sum_{j\ne i}\dfrac{m_j(\mathbf{r}_i - \mathbf{r}_j)}{|\mathbf{r}_i-\mathbf{r}_j|^3}, with \sum_i m_i = 1 and E = T + W = -1/4.
benchmark_equations.schrodinger_or_dirac: N/A: classical dynamics.

systems.notes: The three normalizations are consistent and I verified the chain rather than quoting it: virial equilibrium gives 2T + W = 0, so E = T + W = W/2; with E = -1/4 this gives W = -1/2 and T = 1/4. The virial radius R_{\rm v} \equiv GM^2/(2|W|) = 1/(2\cdot\tfrac12) = 1. From T = \tfrac12 M\langle v^2\rangle = \tfrac14 with M = 1, \langle v^2\rangle = 1/2 and v_{\rm rms} = 1/\sqrt2. Crossing time t_{\rm cr} = 2R_{\rm v}/v_{\rm rms} = 2\sqrt2 \approx 2.83, matching the published value. CAUTION: some papers set E = -1/4 without assuming virial equilibrium, in which case R_{\rm v} \ne 1 and the third generator must be read from E, not R; others normalize R_{\rm v} = 1 and let E float. The two agree only in virial equilibrium; prefer the E = -1/4 binding when both are stated and conflict.

systems.name: Ephemeris units and the TDB/TCB time-scale rescaling
systems.used_in: Planetary and lunar ephemerides (JPL DE4xx, INPOP, EPM), pulsar timing (TEMPO2, PINT, IPTA/NANOGrav), spacecraft navigation and radio science, relativistic celestial mechanics, VLBI and reference-frame work.

per_symbol_rescalings.symbol: the second (and every quantity built on it)
per_symbol_rescalings.relation: TDB = TCB - L_B(\mathrm{JD_{TCB}} - T_0)\times86400 + \mathrm{TDB_0}, with L_B = 1.550519768\times10^{-8}. A TDB-compatible quantity is smaller than its TCB-compatible counterpart by the factor (1 - L_B).
per_symbol_rescalings.why: TDB is a linearly rescaled version of TCB, so 'the second' denotes two different intervals in the two scales. A genuine unit rescaling by a dimensionless factor, invisible to dimensional analysis, silently propagating into every derived constant.

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: \mathrm{au_{TDB}} = \mathrm{au_{TCB}}(1 - L_B)
per_symbol_rescalings.why: Ephemeris length scales inherit the time-scale rescaling. Pre-2012 ephemerides quote a TDB-compatible au differing from the TCB-compatible one in the eighth significant figure.

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: (GM)_{\rm TDB} = (GM)_{\rm TCB}(1 - L_B)
per_symbol_rescalings.why: Same cascade. Mixing a TCB-compatible GM with TDB-compatible positions produces an error of order 1.5e-8, far above modern ephemeris precision.

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: TT = TCG - L_G(\mathrm{JD_{TCG}} - T_0)\times86400, with L_G = 6.969290134\times10^{-10} (a defining constant)
per_symbol_rescalings.why: The same structure one level down, relating geocentric coordinate time to terrestrial time; relevant for Earth-orbiting and geodetic applications.

systems.notes: PRECISELY WHY THIS IS UNSUPPORTED. (1) A magnitude is the logarithm of a RATIO of fluxes, hence dimensionless, so no meaningful (M,L,T,\Theta,I) exponent tuple exists — the dimensional formalism has nothing to bite on. (2) The map from flux to magnitude is not linear, so the linear-algebra restoration that defines this engine does not apply: sums of magnitudes are products of fluxes and differences are ratios. (3) Dimensional homogeneity checking is meaningless: m = -2.5\log_{10}f_\nu - 48.60 takes the logarithm of a dimensionful quantity, defined only because a zero point has been silently divided out. (4) The zero point is a per-system convention (AB, ST, Vega, plus per-instrument variants), so two magnitudes in the same band are not comparable without it. RECOMMENDED BEHAVIOR: detect 'mag' or 'dex' and refuse dimension-checking with a specific message, then offer a SEPARATE logarithmic-unit converter requiring an explicit zero point and band, converting mag to a flux density with a declared dimension before re-entering the dimensional formalism — the same treatment decibels, pH and Richter magnitudes need. I verified both zero points arithmetically: 3631 Jy = 3.631e-20 erg s^-1 cm^-2 Hz^-1 and -2.5 log10(3.631e-20) = 48.600; f_lambda = 3.631e-9 erg s^-1 cm^-2 A^-1 gives -2.5 log10(3.631e-9) = 21.100. Additional trap: 'dex' means both a unit of a logarithm (a factor of 10) and loosely 'orders of magnitude', and [Fe/H] is a log ratio-of-ratios relative to solar — doubly relative.
